quote: Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
rationale: Vendor gives a full IP indemnity plus indemnities for breach of law, bodily injury/property damage, Customer Data breaches and gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud, with standard procedure (§20.4) and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies (§20.5); Customer's indemnity is narrowly limited to its own material and unlawful use. Indemnities also sit outside the liability cap as Excluded Claims, so no super-cap is needed.

quote: Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel.
rationale: We own Customer Data and our pre-existing IP (§14.1), we own and receive an assignment of Deliverables (§14.2), Vendor Technology stays with Vendor but is covered by the perpetual §13.2 licence (§14.3), and no joint ownership is created (§14.4). No Customer IP or data is assigned to Vendor.

quote: Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
rationale: Section 21 matches our preferred position: mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, mutual consequential-damages exclusion, and uncapped Excluded Claims for confidentiality, data-protection/security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, with Customer's payment obligation excluded from the cap. "Fees" (§1.5) is a real revenue base, so the cap is not illusory.

rationale: Preferred position met: we may assign freely to Affiliates and successors, Vendor needs our consent (including on change of control) and may never assign to a competitor, and §24.4 confirms our change of control gives Vendor no termination, repricing or suspension right.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot commit to a sole-supplier arrangement, and this clause also contradicts Section 12.3, so we have deleted it. If some protection is needed we could look at exclusivity for one defined product category for 12 months, ending automatically if service levels are missed.

quote: Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
rationale: This is exclusive dealing for the entire three-year term with no performance-based exit, which is walk-away territory and also contradicts Section 12.3. We propose deleting it; if protection is needed, we could accept exclusivity for a defined category for 12 months ending automatically on missed service levels.

rationale: This is an uncapped daily penalty payable by us triggered by any delay in a dependency, however minor — outside even the fallback (a 3-month early-termination fee). We propose deletion; Vendor's remedy for our delay should be schedule relief.

rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction binds us; Section 12.3 expressly confirms our freedom to develop, acquire, sell and operate in any field or territory. (The exclusivity and non-solicit clauses in §2.2 and §12.4 are addressed under their own rules.)

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement runs for three years with no Customer right to exit without cause, so we have added a convenience right on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees.

ops.text: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination and no early-termination charge applies.

proposal.summary: Add Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice

quote: Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an affected Order Form for the other Party's material breach if the breach remains uncured thirty days after written notice describing it in reasonable detail.
rationale: Section 9 provides only cause-based termination (breach, insolvency, security/service failures) and the term is three years, so we have no convenience exit — a deviation. We have inserted a new §9.4 allowing Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees; Vendor has no convenience right, which is correct.

ops.newText: Vendor may audit Customer's use of the Services no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, through an independent auditor bound by confidentiality obligations. Vendor and its auditor have no right of access to Customer's systems, and Customer may satisfy an audit by providing usage records.
ops.oldText: Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.

proposal.summary: Limit audits to once a year on 30 days' notice; delete remote system access

quote: Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
rationale: Unlimited, unannounced audits with remote access to our systems is expressly walk-away territory and also conflicts with §22.2's no-direct-access language. We have limited audits to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice by an independent auditor with no system access; the §22.2 cost allocation (Vendor pays unless underpayment exceeds 5%) already meets our position.

This does not restrict general advertisements or other recruitment efforts not targeted at such personnel, or the hiring of any person who responds to them or approaches a Party on an unsolicited basis.

We have narrowed it to a mutual 12-month non-solicit for personnel involved in the Services with the usual carve-outs.
